liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let it Grow** (2 reviews): Called an epic version; Garcia's solo is singled out as astonishing, worth replaying [19][23]
- **Althea** (1 review): Described as sweet in the first set [19]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Garcia plays strong solos while Brent drives it on Hammond organ [19]
- **Ship of Fools** (1 review): Reviewer particularly likes this version [25]
- **Space** (1 review): Phil's very spaced-out playing in Space is singled out as reason enough to hear the show [22]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Sugar Magnolia into Playin' into Sunshine Daydream is called a rare, strong sequence [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-04-18.beyerm160.unknown.andrewf.82487.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 171 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape damage is audible in Cold Rain & Snow, and a low PA hum runs through much of set two [1]
- **gd1982-04-18.169231.senn441.fox.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 173 min [6]
- **gd1982-04-18.155703.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 170 min [8]
- **gd82-04-18.sbd.miller.18116.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 165 min; rated 3.92/5 by 24 [10]. Said about its sound: Soundboard has a well-balanced mix; An audience recording also exists, and next to it this soundboard sounds muffled, as if underwater; Soundboard captures Phil's Earthquake details better, but the audience tape gives a fuller space jam [17][24][25]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, a Simsbury High School senior, paid $11.50 for reserved seats; seats behind the stage cost $8 [20]
- Reviewer has long called this the Earthquake show [20]
- Reviewer rates both the show and its mix above Dick's Picks 32 [17]
- The previous night had a notable Shakedown and a Baby Blue encore [20]
- The Don't Ease Me In encore had also been played on the band's previous spring visit [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-04-18.beyerm160.unknown.andrewf.82487.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise (?); transferred by Andrew F.; source: Beyers M160's > Sony TC-D5, near the Sbd > MAC [1]. Also: Cuts and a tape flip during Drums were patched using another source, ShnID-14487 [1]
- **gd1982-04-18.169231.senn441.fox.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Larry Fox, Tim McKenzie; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Larry Fox's Master FOB Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics> Sony TC-D5M (metal tape master)> Tim McKenzie's 1st generation cassettes (TDK SA-90, no Dolby) [6]. Also: Sennheiser 421 and Beyer M160 sources were combined to supply an 8:14 patch in Drums [6]
- **gd1982-04-18.155703.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes ; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [8]. Also: An audience source from andrew f supplies a 4:19 patch in Drums; Joe B. Jones verified the pitch [8]
- **gd82-04-18.sbd.miller.18116.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-04-18 Hartford Civic Center, Hartford, CT, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-04-18-hartford-civic-center-hartford-ct-usa/) [27]
- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-04-17 Hartford Civic Center, Hartford, CT, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-04-17-hartford-civic-center-hartford-ct-usa/) [28]
- Poster by Visible Vibrations: [Grateful Dead Backstage Pass Hartford 1982 Jerry Garcia Red | Visible Vibrations](https://visiblevibrations.com/product/grateful-dead-backstage-pass-jerry-garcia-1982-hartford-red/) [29]
